articles.title: Liquid Gold Rush: How Ghee Became a $62 Billion Global Phenomenon — and Why Your Nani Saw It Coming
articles.excerpt: North America is now the fastest-growing ghee market in the world, driven by keto diets, Ayurvedic wellness trends, and a diaspora that never stopped cooking with it.
articles.image_caption: A jar of golden homemade ghee, the traditional Indian clarified butter
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up watching their grandmothers simmer butter into liquid gold, the West's sudden obsession with ghee is both vindicating and a little amusing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Darjeeling to 2,000 Walmarts: Indian Tea Gets Its Zero-Tariff American Moment
articles.excerpt: A new US-India trade deal eliminates duties on Indian tea, giving exporters a competitive edge over China just as brands like Vahdam are scaling up coast to coast.
articles.image_caption: A Darjeeling tea garden in the misty hills of West Bengal, India — source of the world's most prized tea leaves
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who have long wished they could get real Indian tea at the corner store instead of settling for generic blends, the surge of Indian tea brands into mainstream US retail hits close to home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Kulfi Effect: How Indian Ice Cream Is Winning Over America, One Saffron Scoop at a Time
articles.excerpt: From Malai's masala chai scoops in Manhattan to Kesar Creamery's gulab jamun gelato in Texas, Indian-inspired ice cream brands are reshaping the American frozen dessert landscape — and making NRIs feel right at home.
articles.image_caption: Traditional malai kulfi garnished with pistachios, served on a plate
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American entrepreneurs are bringing the tastes of home — kulfi, falooda, saffron pistachio — to mainstream American ice cream shops, giving NRIs nostalgic flavours and normalising Indian desserts for a wider audience.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Baked Oats Chaat to Rasmalai Tres Leches: India's Viral Fusion Recipes Are Rewriting the Global Cookbook
articles.excerpt: A new generation of Indian food creators is mashing up dosa with gochujang, rasmalai with tres leches, and ragi with chocolate lava cake — and racking up tens of millions of views in the process.
articles.image_caption: A colourful plate of papri chaat topped with chutneys, yogurt, and crispy sev
articles.nri_angle: NRI home cooks are recreating India's viral fusion recipes with ingredients from Patel Brothers and Amazon, adapting them to American kitchens and contributing to a global feedback loop that is making Indian food culture more dynamic than ever.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From a Family Clay Oven to a James Beard Nod: The Immigrant Story Behind Las Vegas's Hottest Indian Restaurant
articles.excerpt: Tamba — named for the Hindi word for copper — earned a Best New Restaurant finalist nod from the James Beard Foundation in its first year, capping a three-decade journey that began with an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant.
articles.image_caption: A traditional tandoor clay oven, the centrepiece of Indian cooking that gave the Dhillon family's first restaurant its name
articles.nri_angle: Tamba's journey from an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant to a James Beard Best New Restaurant finalist mirrors the larger arc of Indian cuisine's ascent in America, offering diaspora families a powerful narrative of generational ambition rewarded.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Britannia, Bikano, and Beyond: Indian Snack Brands Storm the American Grocery Aisle
articles.excerpt: From Walmart's $10 billion India sourcing pledge to Truly Indian's 1,300-store blitz, packaged Indian food is carving out shelf space that restaurants alone never could.
articles.image_caption: Indian packaged snacks — brands like Britannia, Bikano, and Haldiram's are expanding aggressively into American grocery aisles
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who once drove 45 minutes to the nearest desi grocery store for a packet of Good Day biscuits, seeing Britannia and Bikano on Walmart shelves is nothing short of a cultural arrival.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Haldi Doodh to Herb of the Year: How India's Golden Spice Conquered American Wellness
articles.excerpt: The International Herb Association has crowned turmeric the 2026 Herb of the Year, completing a journey from Indian grandmothers' kitchens to Whole Foods shelves and $7 lattes.
articles.image_caption: Vibrant golden turmeric powder, the spice crowned 2026 Herb of the Year
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up being force-fed haldi doodh, watching turmeric become a $7 cafe latte and official Herb of the Year is a bittersweet vindication of the traditions they once dismissed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Fake Dosa Makers: How AI-Generated Videos Are Weaponising Indian Street Food
articles.excerpt: Millions of views, zero reality — AI-generated clips depicting unsanitary Indian food preparation are going viral, and the diaspora is paying the reputational price.
articles.image_caption: Sev puri chaat, a real Indian street food dish — vibrant, hygienic, and made with craft
articles.nri_angle: AI-generated fake videos depicting unsanitary Indian food preparation are fuelling anti-Indian stereotypes online, undercutting the diaspora's decades-long effort to gain respect for Indian cuisine in the West.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The $24 Bag of Rice: How US Tariffs Are Reshaping the Desi Pantry
articles.excerpt: With US duties on Indian goods at 50 percent, staples from Sona Masoori rice to filter coffee have surged in price — and Pakistani brands are quietly filling the gap.
articles.image_caption: Basmati rice, a staple of the Indian diaspora pantry now facing steep US tariff hikes (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The 50 percent US tariff on Indian goods is directly hitting NRI family budgets, turning everyday pantry staples like rice, dal, and coffee into luxury items.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Pani Puri to Prix Fixe: Sujan Sarkar's Michelin Empire Lands in New York and Phoenix
articles.excerpt: The first Bengali chef to earn a Michelin star in America opens two restaurants in five weeks, stretching Indian fine dining from Hudson Yards to the Arizona desert.
articles.image_caption: Pani puri served at an Indian restaurant, a dish Sarkar has reimagined as an oyster course
articles.nri_angle: Sarkar's expansion from Chicago to New York and Phoenix proves Indian fine dining is now viable beyond coastal food capitals, giving NRIs across America access to world-class Indian cuisine.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chicken Stock in Dal Makhani? A Former MasterChef Judge Just Ignited Indian Food's Loudest Fight
articles.excerpt: George Calombaris's Instagram reel adding chicken stock cubes to dal makhani has reignited the perennial debate over who gets to reinterpret Indian classics — and where the red line sits.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of traditional dal makhani garnished with cream and fresh coriander
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up eating their mother's dal makhani, the controversy touches a nerve about cultural ownership and whether Western chefs dilute Indian food's identity as it goes global.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From a Hotel Lobby in Fort Collins to a Strip Mall in Columbus: Indian Food Is Showing Up Everywhere
articles.excerpt: A new wave of Indian restaurants is quietly spreading into mid-sized American cities far from the coastal corridors, driven by immigrant families betting on untapped appetites.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Indian thali with an assortment of dishes — Indian restaurants are popping up in unexpected American cities from Fort Collins to Columbus
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs living outside traditional desi enclaves, these openings signal that Indian food is becoming accessible in the kinds of cities where finding a decent biryani once meant a two-hour drive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tandoori on the Grill: How the Desi Fourth of July Became a Diaspora Tradition
articles.excerpt: This Independence Day, Indian Americans are bringing tikka marinades, masala corn, and chutney sliders to the backyard cookout — reshaping what the all-American BBQ looks like
articles.image_caption: Tandoori chicken on the grill — a scene increasingly common at Indian American Fourth of July cookouts

articles.title: The Beard's New Palate: Indian Cuisine's Record Run at America's Most Prestigious Food Awards
articles.excerpt: From Chai Pani to Tamba to Cal-India Collective, a record number of South Asian finalists at the 2026 James Beard Awards signals a seismic shift in how America eats

articles.title: Vacuum-Sealed Nostalgia: The Gujarati Home Kitchens Feeding America's NRIs
articles.excerpt: In Mumbai and Ahmedabad, a network of women entrepreneurs is vacuum-packing thepla, khakhra, and fafda for suitcase-bound NRIs — and the business is booming
articles.image_caption: A traditional Gujarati snack spread — the kind of comfort food that travels thousands of miles in vacuum-sealed packages to NRI doorsteps
